title: fix: add Koa Request type augmentation for body and rawBody
body:
## Summary

`tsc --noEmit` was failing because `body` and `rawBody` don't exist on Koa's `Request` type. These properties are injected at runtime by `koa-bodyparser`, and `@types/koa-bodyparser` normally augments Koa's `Request` interface to match. However, `tsconfig.json` sets `"types": ["node"]` to prevent `@types/koa-bodyparser`'s bundled `@types/koa`/`@types/node` from conflicting with the project's own copies — which also suppresses the augmentation.

**Fix**: Added `src/server/web-server/koa-bodyparser.d.ts` — a local module augmentation that declares `body` and `rawBody` on Koa's `Request` interface, picked up automatically since `tsconfig.json` includes `src/`.

```ts
export {};

declare module "koa" {
  interface Request {
    body?: unknown;
    rawBody: string;
  }
}
```

Fix with Copilot: https://github.com/counterfact/api-simulator/actions/runs/30681583781/job/91319534656

title: fix: include path-item-level parameters in generated TypeScript types and server runtime
body:
## Summary

OpenAPI allows parameters to be defined at the path item level (shared across all operations on that path), but both the TypeScript generator and the server dispatcher only read operation-level parameters — causing `path: never` in generated route handler types and missing type conversion (e.g. integer coercion) at runtime when parameters were declared at the path item level.

**Root cause (type generator):** `buildDollarArgType` called `this.requirement.get("parameters")` which only sees the operation object, never the parent path item.

**Root cause (server):** `operationForPathAndMethod` returned the raw operation object without merging path-item-level parameters, so `parameterTypes()`, `collectExplodedObjectParams()`, and `validateRequest()` all missed those parameters.

**Fix:** Both layers now merge path-item-level and operation-level parameters, with operation-level taking precedence on `name`+`in` collision per the OpenAPI specification. A new `parent` property on `Requirement` makes the path-item navigation direct and avoids URL string parsing. Merge logic in both layers uses a `Map` keyed on `"${in}:${name}"` for a clean O(n) implementation.

```yaml
# Before fix: generates `path: never` and skips integer coercion at runtime
paths:
  /stuff/{stuffId}:
    parameters:
      - name: stuffId
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
    get:
      responses:
        '204':
          description: successful
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

Parameters defined on the path level are ignored. The generated type in `types/paths/stuff/{stuffId}.types.ts` has `path: never` even though there should be the `stuffId` path parameter.

Parameters on path level are defined here: https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.1.2.md#fixed-fields-7

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] A spec with `parameters` defined only at the path item level generates a non-`never` `path` type in the corresponding `types/paths/…types.ts` file
- [x] A spec with parameters at both path item level and operation level produces merged types, with the operation-level entry overriding the path-level one when they share the same `name` and `in`
- [x] A spec with parameters only at the operation level continues to generate correct types (no regression)
- [x] At runtime, an integer parameter defined at the path item level is correctly coerced from a URL string to a number before being passed to the handler
- [x] Required parameters defined at the path item level are validated on incoming requests (missing parameter returns 400)

## Tasks

- Added `getEffectiveParameters()` to `OperationTypeCoder` — uses `this.requirement.parent` to access the path item requirement directly, merges path-item-level and operation-level parameter arrays using a `Map`
- Updated `buildDollarArgType` to call `getEffectiveParameters()` instead of `this.requirement.get("parameters")`
- Changed `import type { Requirement }` → `import { Requirement }` to allow constructing the merged `Requirement` instance
- Added `public parent: Requirement | undefined` property to `Requirement`; `get()` now sets `child.parent = this` so any consumer can navigate to the logical parent without URL string parsing
- Added unit tests for `Requirement.parent`: child parent is set by `get()`, root has no parent, `select()` chains parents correctly
- Added two new unit tests for the type generator: path-item-only params generate non-`never` path type; operation-level params override path-level on same `name`+`in`
- Updated `OpenApiDocument.paths` in `dispatcher.ts` to type path items with an optional `parameters?: OpenApiParameters[]` field
- Rewrote `mergeParameters()` in `dispatcher.ts` using a `Map<string, OpenApiParameters>` keyed on `"${in}:${name}"` (operation-level naturally overrides path-level on duplicate key)
- Replaced `findOperation()` with `findPathItem()`; `operationForPathAndMethod()` now merges path-item parameters into the returned operation so type conversion, exploded query param reconstruction, and request validation all honour path-item-level parameters
- Added two new dispatcher tests: path-item-only integer coercion; merge of path-item and operation-level parameters
- Added changeset (patch)

title: fix: cast OAS3 schema-typed parameters at runtime
body:
## Summary

OAS3 places parameter types under `parameter.schema.type` rather than the OAS2 top-level `parameter.type`. The dispatcher's `parameterTypes()` only read the OAS2 field, so path/query/header parameters declared OAS3-style were never cast — e.g. `$.path.petId` remained `"1"` (string) instead of `1` (number).

**Fix:** one-line fallback in `Dispatcher.parameterTypes()`:

```ts
// Before
const type = parameter?.type;

// After
const type = parameter?.type ?? parameter?.schema?.type;
```

**Test:** new dispatcher test mirrors the existing OAS2 casting test but uses `schema: { type: "integer" }` etc. to cover the OAS3 path end-to-end.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

When a parameter is not a string per the OpenAPI spec the server should perform type conversions as necessary.

For example when GET /pet/1 is called, $.path.petId should be a number not a string.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `GET /pet/1` where `petId` is declared as OAS3 `schema: { type: "integer" }` — `$.path.petId` is the number `1`, not the string `"1"`
- [ ] `GET /pets?limit=10` where `limit` is declared as OAS3 `schema: { type: "integer" }` — `$.query.limit` is the number `10`, not `"10"`
- [ ] A header declared `schema: { type: "boolean" }` with raw value `"true"` arrives as the boolean `true` in the handler
- [ ] OAS2-style `type: "integer"` path/query/header parameters still cast correctly (regression)
- [ ] String parameters remain strings under both OAS2 and OAS3 declaration styles

## Tasks

- Fixed `Dispatcher.parameterTypes()` in `src/server/dispatcher.ts` to fall back to `parameter.schema?.type` when `parameter.type` is absent
- Added a new test in `test/server/dispatcher.test.ts` covering OAS3 schema-typed path, query, and header parameter casting
- Added a patch changeset

title: Fix: Query params of type object are now exploded correctly (OpenAPI default)
body:
## Summary

OpenAPI 3.x defaults query parameters of type `object` to `style: form, explode: true`, which means each property is sent as its own query param (e.g. `?page=0&size=100&sort=name`). Counterfact was looking for the literal parameter name (`pageable`) in the query string, producing a false 400 "required" error and never assembling the object for the handler.

**Validation** (`src/server/request-validator.ts`)
- Added `isExplodedObjectQueryParam()` — detects object-type query params using the OpenAPI 3.x default serialisation rules (`style: form`, `explode: true`)
- `findMissingRequired()` now considers a required object param satisfied when any of its schema-declared properties appear in the query string

**Object reconstruction** (`src/server/dispatcher.ts`)
- Added `collectExplodedObjectParams()` — gathers flat query keys that match a parameter's schema properties back under the parameter name before the handler is called
- Handler receives `$.query.pageable = { page: "0", size: "100" }` instead of bare `$.query.page` etc.
- Unrelated query params remain at the top level of `$.query`

**Type updates** (`src/counterfact-types/open-api-parameters.ts`)
- Added `style?: string`, `explode?: boolean`, and `properties` to `OpenApiParameters` so the checks are type-safe

Setting `explode: false` on a parameter in the spec opts out of this behaviour and restores the previous lookup-by-name semantics.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

**Bug: Query Params of Type Object do not explode**

When a query parameter is declared with a schema of `type: object` (e.g. `Pageable` with `page`, `size`, `sort`), calling the endpoint with exploded properties (`?page=0&size=100&sort=a`) returns:

> Request validation failed: query parameter 'pageable' is required

According to the OpenAPI spec, `in: query` parameters default to `style: form, explode: true`, so each object property should map to its own query param. The validator incorrectly expects a literal `pageable` key. Setting `style: form, explode: true` explicitly has no effect.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] `GET /test?page=0&size=100` no longer returns 400 when `pageable` is a required object-type query parameter
- [x] The handler receives `$.query.pageable` as a reconstructed object (`{ page: "0", size: "100" }`) rather than having those keys only at the top level
- [x] Sending no `pageable` properties when the parameter is `required: true` still returns 400 mentioning the parameter name
- [x] A query parameter with `explode: false` in the spec is still resolved by its own name (no regression)
- [x] Unrelated query params not in the object schema remain accessible directly on `$.query`

## Tasks

- Added `isExplodedObjectQueryParam()` to `request-validator.ts` (exported) and wired it into `findMissingRequired()`
- Added `collectExplodedObjectParams()` to `dispatcher.ts`; applied it between validation and handler dispatch
- Broadened `DispatcherRequest.query` to `string | string[]` to match Koa's actual parsed type
- Updated `OpenApiParameters` with `style`, `explode`, and `schema.properties`
- Added 4 new tests covering acceptance, rejection, reconstruction, and preservation of unrelated params
- Added patch changeset and documented exploded object query params in `docs/features/routes.md`

title: Handle `_.context` syntax/import failures without crashing startup
body:
## Summary

A broken `_.context.ts` (syntax/import error) previously bubbled into startup failure paths. This change makes context-module load failures non-fatal: Counterfact now warns and skips that context module, while continuing to load routes.

- **Context load error handling**
  - In `ModuleLoader.loadEndpoint`, context files (`_.context.*`) now take a dedicated error path on import failure.
  - Instead of registering route-style 500 handlers or throwing, loader writes a warning and returns.
- **Route error behavior unchanged**
  - Non-context route modules still keep existing behavior (500 responder registration for import/syntax failures).
- **Docs update**
  - Added explicit note in state docs that invalid `_.context.ts` is skipped with a warning.
- **Release metadata**
  - Added a patch changeset describing the behavior change.

```ts
if (this.isContextFile(pathName)) {
  const warning = isSyntaxError
    ? `Warning: There is a syntax error in the context file: ${displayPath}`
    : `Warning: There was an error loading the context file: ${displayPath}`;

  process.stdout.write(`\n${warning}\n`);
  return;
}
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

**Issue title:** App should not crash due to syntax error in _.context.ts

**Issue description:** A syntax error in _.context.ts should not cause the app to crash. Instead it should print a warning and not load the context module.

</details>

title: Add runtime response header validation with OpenAPI hot-reload
body:
## Summary

Validates response headers at runtime against the OpenAPI spec and reports errors as `response-type-error` HTTP headers — one header per error, with the same name repeated for multiple errors. Enabled by default; disable with `--no-validate-response`. Changes to the OpenAPI spec file are picked up automatically without a server restart.

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] Start counterfact against a spec with a required response header; call the route without setting it — verify a `response-type-error` header describes the missing header

title: fix: type error when returning a response with no body
fix: escape XML special characters in jsonToXml text content
body:
## Problem

In `src/server/json-to-xml.ts`, the `jsonToXml` function escapes attribute values via `xmlEscape()` but does **not** escape text content in the fallback branch for primitive values:

```ts
return `<${name}>${String(json)}</${name}>`;
```

If the string contains `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` or ``, the output will be malformed XML. For example, `jsonToXml("<script>alert(1)</script>", undefined, "data")` produces `<data><script>alert(1)</script></data>` — broken XML.

## Fix

Apply the existing `xmlEscape()` function to `String(json)` in the text content branch:

```ts
return `<${name}>${xmlEscape(String(json))}</${name}>`;
```

## Testing

Added two new test cases:
- Escaping `<script>alert("xss")</script>` in text content
- Escaping `&`, `<`, `>` in a mixed string

Fixes #1739

title: Fix Tools.accepts() failing when Accept header has spaces after commas
body:
`Tools.accepts()` incorrectly returned `false` for valid Accept headers like `"text/html, application/json"` because tokens weren't trimmed after splitting on `","`, leaving a leading space that broke the type comparison.

## Summary

Single-char fix: `.trim()` each token before splitting on `"/"`.

```ts
// Before
const [type, subtype] = acceptType.split("/");
// After
const [type, subtype] = acceptType.trim().split("/");
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`Tools.accepts()` splits on `","` but does not trim whitespace from each part. This produces `[" application/json"]` (with a leading space) as the second element. When that is further split on `"/"`, the type becomes `" application"` rather than `"application"`, so the comparison always fails and `accepts()` returns `false` even when the type is listed in the Accept header.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `Tools.accepts('application/json')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/html, application/json"` (space after comma)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('text/html')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/html"` (no change to single-type behavior)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('text/html')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/*"` (wildcard subtype still works)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('application/json')` returns `false` when Accept header is `"text/*"` (rejection still works)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('what/ever')` returns `true` when Accept header is `undefined` (missing header still accepts all)

## Tasks

- Added `.trim()` to each `acceptType` token before splitting on `"/"` in `src/server/tools.ts`
- Added test case for space-separated Accept header to the `it.each` truth table in `test/server/tools.test.ts`

title: fix: Tools.accepts() case-insensitive accept header lookup
body:
`Tools.accepts()` read `this.headers.Accept` (capital A), but Node.js normalizes all incoming HTTP header names to lowercase. In production, `this.headers.Accept` is always `undefined`, triggering the early-return guard and making `accepts()` unconditionally return `true`.

## Summary

Replace the direct key lookup with a case-insensitive search so `accept`, `Accept`, and `ACCEPT` all resolve correctly.

```ts
// Before — broken in production (Node.js lowercases all headers)
const acceptHeader = this.headers.Accept;

// After — handles any casing
const acceptHeader = Object.entries(this.headers).find(
  ([key]) => key.toLowerCase() === "accept",
)?.[1];
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`Tools.accepts()` reads `this.headers.Accept` (capital A). Node.js normalises all incoming HTTP header names to **lowercase**, so when a real HTTP request is processed via Koa the header is stored under `accept` (lowercase). `this.headers.Accept` is therefore always `undefined` in production.

Because `undefined` triggers the early-return guard `if (acceptHeader === "" || acceptHeader === undefined) { return true; }`, the method unconditionally returns `true` — completely ignoring the client's actual Accept header.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `Tools.accepts("application/json")` returns `false` when the request carries a lowercase `accept: text/plain` header
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("text/html")` returns `true` when the request carries `accept: text/html`
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("text/html")` returns `true` when the request carries `Accept: text/html` (capital A, e.g. from a browser or curl)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("application/json")` returns `true` when no `accept` header is present (existing permissive behavior unchanged)
- [ ] A route handler that gates response type on `tools.accepts()` returns `406 Not Acceptable` when the client sends an incompatible `accept` header in a real Koa request

## Tasks

- Added failing test: `accepts('application/json') returns false when lowercase 'accept' header is 'text/plain'`
- Replaced `this.headers.Accept` with a case-insensitive `Object.entries()` lookup in `src/server/tools.ts`

title: Fix: Dispatcher proxy() always throws when request body is present
body:
`proxy()` in the Dispatcher was broken in two ways: `headers.contentType` (camelCase) was used instead of `headers["content-type"]` (kebab-case), causing the guard to always evaluate as `true`; and the guard itself unnecessarily restricted proxying to `application/json` requests only.

## Summary

Remove the content-type restriction from `proxy()` entirely so it works for all content types. Rather than re-serializing the parsed body, `proxy()` now forwards `ctx.request.rawBody` — the original wire bytes stored by `koa-bodyparser` before parsing — directly to `fetch()`. This eliminates all re-serialization and correctly handles every content type, including those with charset suffixes (e.g. `application/json; charset=utf-8`).

```ts
// Before (broken — threw for every request with a body)
if (body !== undefined && headers.contentType !== "application/json") {
  throw new Error(`$.proxy() is currently limited to application/json requests...`);
}
body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),

// After — no restriction, no re-serialization; raw wire bytes forwarded as-is
body: body === undefined ? undefined : rawBody,
```

`koa-bodyparser` unconditionally sets `returnRawBody: true` on `co-body` internally, so `ctx.request.rawBody` is always available as the unparsed string for any request that has a body.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`proxy()` in the Dispatcher had a guard that threw when the request body was present and the content-type was not `application/json`. The guard used `headers.contentType` (camelCase) instead of `headers["content-type"]` (kebab-case), so it was always `undefined`, making the condition always `true` — causing `proxy()` to throw for every request carrying a body, including valid `application/json` POSTs.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/json` and a JSON body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and a JSON body successfully proxies through (charset suffix handled correctly)
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: text/plain` and a plain-text body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and a body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `GET /any-route` with no body proxies normally (unchanged behavior)
- [ ] The upstream response body and headers are returned correctly regardless of content type

## Tasks

- Remove the content-type restriction guard from `proxy()` in `src/server/dispatcher.ts`
- Add `rawBody?: string` to `DispatcherRequest` type
- In `koa-middleware.ts`, declare `rawBody` on the Koa `Request` interface, destructure `ctx.request.rawBody`, and pass it through to `dispatcher.request()` (excluded for GET/HEAD, consistent with `body`)
- In `dispatcher.ts`, destructure `rawBody` in `request()` and use `body === undefined ? undefined : rawBody` in `proxy()` — no re-serialization of any kind
- Update tests: pass `rawBody` alongside `body` and verify the exact string forwarded to upstream `fetch` is the raw wire bytes unchanged

title: Improve error messages for malformed OpenAPI specs
body:
## Summary

A bad or partial OpenAPI document produced a raw JavaScript stack trace instead of a user-facing message. This replaces those stack traces with clear, actionable errors that include the spec path and the underlying cause.

**Before:**
```
ResolverError: Error opening file /path/to/bad-spec.yaml: ENOENT: no such file or directory
    at Object.read (node_modules/@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser/dist/lib/resolvers/file.js:74:19)
    at ...
```

**After:**
```
❌ Could not load the OpenAPI spec from "bad-spec.yaml".
Error opening file /path/to/bad-spec.yaml: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/path/to/bad-spec.yaml'
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

A bad or partial OpenAPI document currently produces a JavaScript stack trace, not a user-facing message pointing at the problem. Given that users feed arbitrary specs to this tool, clear, actionable errors at this boundary would meaningfully reduce friction.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Running `counterfact nonexistent.yaml ./api` prints a `❌` message containing the spec path and a clear reason (e.g. ENOENT), with no stack trace
- [x] Running with a spec that has a broken `$ref` (pointing to a missing file) prints a user-friendly error, not a raw exception

## Tasks

- **`app.ts`** — `loadOpenApiDocument()` throws the same friendly error format instead of silently returning `undefined`; `counterfact()` and `start()` skip spec loading and code generation/watching when `openApiPath === "_"` (run-without-spec mode); removed now-dead `undefined` guard in `createMswHandlers()`

title: Fix: syntax error in a route file no longer crashes the server
body:
A syntax error in a CommonJS route file would crash Counterfact via an unhandled promise rejection. `require()` throws synchronously on parse failure; the existing `.catch()` only handled promise rejections, so the error re-threw past `void loadEndpoint(...)`.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `uncached-require.cjs` called `require()` synchronously inside `Promise.resolve(...)`, so a `SyntaxError` escaped before `.catch()` could intercept it. The outer `catch` re-threw, producing an unhandled rejection.

**Fix:**
- **`uncached-require.cjs`** — wrap `require()` in `try/catch`, return `Promise.reject(error)` on failure so errors are always promise rejections
- **`module-loader.ts` (`loadEndpoint`)** — capture import errors and register a stub `Module` for all HTTP methods that returns `500` with an informative message:
  - `SyntaxError` → `"There is a syntax error in the route file: <path>"`
  - Other errors → `"There was an error loading the route file: <path>"`
- When the file is fixed and the watcher fires again, `registry.add` overwrites the stub with the real handler

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

If a file under `./routes` has a syntax error, Counterfact currently crashes.

The server should not crash. Requests to that route should return a 500 error with a message: "There is a syntax error in the route file: ./routes/my/path.ts"

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Saving a route file with a syntax error (e.g. `const = 1;`) does not crash the server
- [x] A `GET` request to a route whose file has a syntax error returns HTTP 500 with a message containing "syntax error" and the file path
- [x] All other routes continue to respond normally while one route file is broken
- [x] Fixing the syntax error and saving the file causes the route to respond correctly (stub is replaced by real handler)
- [x] A `.cjs` CommonJS route file with a syntax error also returns 500 instead of crashing (this was the primary crash path)
- [x] Deleting a broken route file removes the 500 stub from the registry

## Tasks

- Wrap `require()` in `try/catch` in `uncached-require.cjs` to convert synchronous throws into `Promise.reject`
- Capture import errors in `loadEndpoint` and register a 500 stub module covering all HTTP methods
- Add tests for ESM and CJS route files with syntax errors
- Add changeset entry

title: Fix reserved keyword operationId causing TypeScript syntax errors
body:
## Summary

When an OpenAPI spec uses a JS/TS reserved keyword (e.g. `delete`, `import`, `type`) as an `operationId`, Counterfact emits invalid TypeScript like `import type { delete } from ...`, crashing with a `SyntaxError`. The fix appends `_` to any sanitized identifier that collides with a reserved word.

```ts
// operationId "delete" → "delete_"
export type delete_ = { ... };
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

OpenAPI specs that use reserved words as `operationId` (valid per the spec, accepted by Swagger Editor) caused a `SyntaxError` in generated TypeScript. Example: `operationId: delete` produced `import type { delete } from ...`.

Maintainer direction: append `_` to the identifier and leave an explanatory comment.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] An OpenAPI spec with `operationId: delete` generates valid TypeScript (no `SyntaxError` on import)
- [ ] The generated type name is `delete_` (not `delete`)
- [ ] Other reserved words (`import`, `type`, `return`, etc.) are similarly suffixed with `_`
- [ ] A non-reserved `operationId` like `deleteItem` is unchanged
- [ ] An `operationId` that becomes a reserved word after sanitization (e.g. `delete!!`) is also suffixed
- [ ] Existing operationId sanitization (camelCase, digit prefix) still works correctly

## Tasks

- Added `RESERVED_WORDS` set covering all JS/TS reserved and future-reserved words to `operation-type-coder.js`
- Updated `sanitizeIdentifier` to append `_` when the result is a reserved word
- Added unit tests for direct reserved words, post-sanitization collisions, and non-colliding identifiers

title: Fix TypeError when response content has no schema
body:
## Summary

When a response content entry defines only `examples` (no `schema`), the TypeScript type generator crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'data')` and emits a useless error-comment stub type instead of a valid type.

**Root cause:** `SchemaTypeCoder` was constructed unconditionally with `content.get("schema")`, which returns `undefined` when the key is absent. The coder then blows up accessing `.data` on `undefined`.

**Fix:** Guard with `content.has("schema")` before constructing `SchemaTypeCoder`; fall back to `unknown` when absent.

```js
// Before — crashes when schema is missing
body?: ${new SchemaTypeCoder(content.get("schema")).write(script)}

// After — graceful fallback
body?: ${content.has("schema") ? new SchemaTypeCoder(content.get("schema")).write(script) : "unknown"}
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

When a response lacks a schema (e.g. only has `examples`), the generated type for that operation collapses to an empty `{}` containing only an error comment. This makes the `$` argument in the route handler lose all useful type information (request body, parameters, etc.). The requested behavior is to emit `unknown` for the response body type instead of crashing.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] `POST /stuff` with the issue's spec generates a valid `createStuff` type with `body?: unknown` for the 200 response — no error comment
- [x] The `$` argument in the generated route handler retains meaningful types for request body and parameters when response schema is absent
- [x] Response content that has both `examples` and a `schema` still generates the correctly typed body (no regression)
- [x] Response with no `content` at all still generates `{ status: N }` with no body field
- [x] OpenAPI 2 specs with schema-only responses are unaffected

## Tasks

- Guard `content.has("schema")` before constructing `SchemaTypeCoder` in `operation-type-coder.js` (`responseTypes`)
- Same guard in `response-type-coder.js` (`buildContentObjectType`)
- Unit tests covering the no-schema case in both coders

title: Fix import path for routes containing colons (e.g. `/stuff:action`)
body:
## Summary

Routes with colons in their path (e.g. `/stuff:action`) caused the generated route handler to import from the wrong type file path, making `$` resolve to `any` instead of the correct typed parameter.

**Root cause:** `repository.js` writes files to disk using `escapePathForWindows()`, which replaces `:` with `∶` (U+2236 ratio symbol). But `script.js#importStatements()` computed the import path from the raw unescaped path, producing a mismatch:

```ts
// Before (broken) — file on disk is `stuff∶action.types.js`, import references `stuff:action.types.js`
import type { stuffAction } from "../types/paths/stuff:action.types.js";

// After (fixed) — import matches actual file on disk
import type { stuffAction } from "../types/paths/stuff∶action.types.js";
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

Routes with Colons lead to wrong file import path

While the filenames are generated as expected (with the ratio character instead of the colon character), the import statement in the route file to import the type file is not adjusted properly:

```ts
import type { stuffAction } from "../types/paths/stuff:action.types.js"; // this is a colon, not a ratio
```

This leads to `$` having type `any` which is undesirable.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Generating files from a spec with a colon route (e.g. `/stuff:action`) produces an import path using `∶` (ratio symbol), not `:`
- [x] TypeScript correctly resolves the imported type — `$` is typed, not `any`
- [x] Routes without colons continue to generate correct import paths unchanged
- [x] The generated type file (e.g. `stuff∶action.types.ts`) is written to disk and resolvable by the import in the route handler
- [x] Nested colon paths (e.g. `/category:type/items`) also produce correct import paths

## Tasks

- Applied `escapePathForWindows()` to `resolvedPath` in `Script#importStatements()` (`src/typescript-generator/script.js`)
- Added unit test in `test/typescript-generator/script.test.js` asserting colon is escaped to ratio symbol in generated imports
- Updated snapshot in `test/typescript-generator/__snapshots__/generate.test.ts.snap` to reflect the corrected import path
- Added changeset entry (`patch`)

title: fix: set Content-Type: application/json in RawHttpClient when body is an object
body:
## Summary

`RawHttpClient#send` serialized object bodies to JSON and set `Content-Length`, but never added `Content-Type: application/json`. Without it, `koa-bodyparser` can't identify the payload as JSON, falls through all content-type checks, and returns `{}` — making `$.body` always empty in route handlers when requests originate from the REPL client.

Fix injects `Content-Type: application/json` automatically when the body is a non-null object and the caller hasn't already supplied a `content-type` header:

```ts
// src/repl/RawHttpClient.ts
const effectiveHeaders = { ...headers };

if (
  typeof bodyAsStringOrObject === "object" &&
  bodyAsStringOrObject !== null &&
  !Object.keys(effectiveHeaders).some(
    (k) => k.toLowerCase() === "content-type",
  )
) {
  effectiveHeaders["Content-Type"] = "application/json";
}
```

title: Fix REPL tab completion broken by custom completer overriding Node's built-in
body:
The custom `client.<method>("...")` completer replaced Node's built-in REPL completer entirely, so `context.<Tab>` and all other built-in property completions stopped working.

## Summary

The fix converts the completer to async and threads the built-in REPL completer through as a fallback:

```ts
// Before: custom completer passed at startup, replaces built-in
const replServer = repl.start({ completer: createCompleter(registry), prompt: "⬣> " });

// After: capture built-in first, then wrap it
const replServer = repl.start({ prompt: "⬣> " });
const builtinCompleter = replServer.completer as (line: string, callback: CompleterCallback) => void;
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
(replServer as any).completer = createCompleter(registry, builtinCompleter);
```

`createCompleter` now accepts an optional async `fallback` and returns an `AsyncCompleter`. When input doesn't match the `client.<method>("...")` pattern, it delegates to the fallback instead of returning empty completions.

`@types/node` marks `REPLServer.completer` as readonly, but Node.js sets it as a plain writable instance property in the constructor. The built-in completer is only available after `repl.start()` returns, so it cannot be passed to `repl.start()` directly — we must capture it from the returned instance and replace it with our wrapper via `as any`.

## Manual acceptance tests

title: Fix IfHasKey to use substring matching for content type keys
body:
`MaybeShortcut` (and thus shortcuts like `.json()`) was unavailable when an OpenAPI spec used content types like `application/json; charset=utf-8` because `IfHasKey` required an exact key match.

## Changes

- **`src/counterfact-types/index.ts`** — Changed `IfHasKey` from exact matching (`keyof SomeObject extends FirstKey`) to substring/contains matching (`Extract<keyof SomeObject, \`${string}${FirstKey}${string}\`> extends never`), consistent with how `OmitAll` already works.
- **`test/server/types.test-d.ts`** — Added a type test asserting `IfHasKey` returns `true` when the object has `application/json; charset=utf-8` as a key and the search term is `application/json`.

```ts
// Before: this would resolve to `never` — no `.json()` shortcut available
type R = {
  content: { "application/json; charset=utf-8": { schema: string } };
  headers: {};
  requiredHeaders: never;
};

// After: IfHasKey correctly matches the key, exposing `.json()`
declare const builder: GenericResponseBuilderInner<R>;
builder.json("hello"); // ✅ now works
```

title: Return HTTP 405 when path exists but method is not registered
body:
Previously, any unmatched request returned 404 regardless of whether the URL path existed — making it impossible to distinguish "path not found" from "method not allowed".

## Changes

- **`src/server/dispatcher.ts`**: Added an early-return 405 check in `request()` — if the path is registered but the requested method has no handler, returns 405 with an `Allow` header listing the valid methods; 404 is still returned when the path itself is not found.
- **`src/server/registry.ts`**: Added `ALL_HTTP_METHODS` constant, `pathExistsWithAnyMethod(url, excludeMethod)`, and `allowedMethods(url)` as public methods used by the dispatcher.
- **`test/server/dispatcher.test.ts`**: Added 405 tests for exact paths and wildcard paths.
- **`.changeset/return-405-for-unregistered-methods.md`**: Added a changeset file (type `patch`) to document the change for release management.

## Example

```ts
registry.add("/hello", { GET() { return { body: "hi", status: 200 }; } });

// Before: POST /hello → 404
// After:  POST /hello → 405, Allow: GET
```

title: Fix root middleware not executed for any routes
body:
Root-level `_.middleware.ts` (placed in the `routes/` folder) was silently skipped — it never ran for any route.

The `recurse()` function in `registry.ts` walked path segments from deepest to root by stripping trailing segments, but bottomed out at `""` instead of `"/"`. Since the module-loader registers root middleware under key `"/"`, it was never matched.

**Changes:**
- **`src/server/registry.ts`**: Fix `nextPath` calculation so traversal ends at `"/"` rather than `""`, before terminating at `null`:
  ```ts
  // Before: /devices → "" → null  (never checks "/")
  // After:  /devices → "/" → null  (root middleware matched)
  const nextPath =
    path === "/" || path === ""
      ? null
      : path.slice(0, path.lastIndexOf("/")) || "/";
  ```
- **`test/server/registry.test.ts`**: Update existing middleware tests to register root middleware under `"/"` (consistent with module-loader), and add a focused regression test for the root middleware case.

body:
Fixes #1116 

Counterfact looks at OpenAPI spec to determine the types of parameters in the query, path, or headers and make sure they are parsed to the correct type at runtime (string, number, or boolean -- we don't support arrays yet). 

When using OpenAPI / Swagger v2, the types of parameters are in the `type` property rather than `schema.type`. Counterfact wasn't looking for the `type` property so everything was being left as strings. 

Also, it didn't make a distinction between `number` and `integer`, casting all numbers to integers. With this change integers are parsed with `parseInt()` and numbers are parsed with `parseFloat()`. 

Also booleans were not parsed. Now the string "true" is parsed as `true`; any other string is `false`.
